title: Sicilian Sheet Pan Pizza
seoTitle: Sicilian Sheet Pan Pizza | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Thick focaccia-style squares
description: Thick focaccia-style squares. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Mix soft Sicilian dough
steps.instruction: Bloom yeast in warm water 5 minutes. Mix flour, salt, 2 tbsp oil, and yeast water until a sticky, soft dough forms. Knead 6–8 minutes. Rise 1 hour until puffy — Sicilian is thick and airy, not cracker-thin.

steps.title: Oil pans and press dough
steps.instruction: Oil two 9x13 or half-sheet pans generously. Press dough to fill corners; do not over-stretch thin. Dimple surface with oiled fingertips — those dimples hold olive oil and sauce.

steps.title: Second rise in the pan
steps.instruction: Cover and rise 30–45 minutes until dough looks pillowy and fills the pan edge to edge. Preheat oven to 475°F with racks in lower third.

steps.title: Sauce stripes and cheese
steps.instruction: Whisk crushed tomatoes with garlic and oregano. Spoon sauce in stripes or patches on top — Sicilian often shows dough between sauce. Top with mozzarella, parmesan, and pepperoni if using.

steps.title: Bake until bottom is fried-crisp
steps.instruction: Bake on the lower rack 22–28 minutes until the bottom is deep golden and the center reads 190°F through the cheese. Edges should look fried in oil, not pale steamed bread.

steps.title: Rest and cut squares
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes in the pan, then lift or cut in the pan into squares. Sicilian Sheet Pan Pizza feeds eight from two trays with thick crust and crisp underside — crew grabs with napkins.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Sicilian Sheet Pan Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thick focaccia-style squares. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a 1:1 gluten-free all-purpose flour blend.
